A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same Act2Comm paper, including Appendices A–E. Text and visual inspection support comparison of their equations, figures, tables and appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Act2Comm simulations in Lucky Wheel, Catch the Ball and Erratic Robot, plus appendix ablations, representation comparisons and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results in Section 6 and Appendix D, together with the empirical analyses and ablations in Appendices C and E.

M1.justification: The architecture, quantizer, losses, critic-assisted training and inference procedures are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. Replacing 'gradient descent' with 'gradient ascent' after Equation (10) resolves inconsistent wording: v1 already specifies ascent earlier in Section 4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Lucky Wheel, Catch the Ball and Erratic Robot, retaining the same noisy and noiseless scenarios. No environment, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same comparisons remain: Markov versus history-dependent coding in Figure 12a, scalar versus vector representations in Figure 8a, and component variants in Table 5. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The environment parameters, BER/rate/reward metrics, message lengths, block sizes and training settings remain unchanged in Section 6 and Appendices C–E. Rewording the description of the critic's 20 inner steps does not alter the setting.

E4.justification: Both retain the component, feedback, message-length and target-policy ablations in Appendix E, representation comparison in C.5, and complexity analyses in C.4. Moving Figure 11 and Table 5 does not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Both report averaging performance over 20,000 executions in D.1 and using 10,000 runs for complexity measurements in C.4. No seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results match, including Tables 3–6 and Figures 3–5, 8a and 10–12. For example, Table 6 retains BER 1.06e-3 for k=12, R=1/3 and mu=3. No result entries or reported trends change.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, Lemmas 1–2, their derivations and the unichain assumption are retained. Appendix B replaces dangling 'Assumption 1' references with the existing unichain assumption; reward-argument and EAS-symbol corrections align notation with definitions already present.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about action-state channel capacity, the capacity–reward trade-off and practical Act2Comm coding. No core contribution is added, withdrawn or substantively strengthened.

C2.justification: The finite-block-length feedback explanation added in E.2 repeats an interpretation already stated in v1 Section 5 and Appendix C. Explanations of representation effects, stochastic target policies, scaling limitations and potential multi-agent applicability remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Architectures, hyperparameters, GPU-A5000 disclosure, computational measurements, pseudocode and project/code-access information are retained. Correcting 'Fig.??' to Figure 8b in C.3 repairs navigation to existing details rather than adding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The reference list retains the same works. Section 2 preserves the distinction between prior trajectory-observing source coding and the proposed state-only channel coding; its wording edits do not substantively change the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording, grammar, notation and cross-reference corrections throughout the text and appendices, including the ascent/descent inconsistency and unresolved figure reference. It also adds funding acknowledgments, while retaining the scientific section sequence and narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 3 to page 4, while Figure 11 and Table 5 move from page 26 to page 27. Captions receive small edits and surrounding text reflows; graphical content, axes and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and internal consistency by correcting the ascent/descent wording, notation and broken figure/assumption references. The methods, proofs and empirical evidence remain substantively unchanged, so the supported quality gain is limited to more accurate and navigable presentation.
